fixture_name: Ramp-terminal arterial reconstruction — US preliminary design (MassDOT HSIP municipal RSA, full package)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Substantive safety concern: an undefined two-to-one lane drop with abruptly terminating striping, no advance signage, and observed late merges at the Route 3 NB on-ramp mouth creates a credible merge-vs-turning-vehicle conflict mechanism worth addressing at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (striping ends abruptly, no signage) is supported by verbatim quote EV-US-033; observed merging behavior ties to recorded Safety Issue #2 field observations and RSA-purpose framing cites EV-US-023, with the expectancy mechanism explicitly labelled as inference rather than quoted fact.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics (identifying issues arising from design or operational characteristics per EV-US-023); no compliance/code claim is conflated with the safety issue, and inference is distinguished from evidence.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: install advance merge signage and pavement markings ahead of the on-ramp entrance, plus a viable design alternative (extend two through lanes past the ramp with pre-signed mandatory right-turn trade-off) carried into the ongoing reconstruction — not null and implementable at this stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrian exposure at the adjacent mid-block crosswalk is explicitly considered (driver-attention diversion from the lane drop) and coherently routed to companion finding JB-GF12-001, with a reasoned justification for scoping this finding's conflict mechanism to drivers.
